utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First of all, we put on the record that Mr. Mladic is not present. He has waived his right, and the waiver -- his right to be present, and that waiver has been signed by him and that's filed. Therefore, we'll proceed in the absence of Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was one matter remaining from yesterday. There may be some unclarity as to whether D1335 was formally admitted, whether I spoke the sacred words that they are admitted. Most likely, I did not. Therefore, D1335 - which I think appears already in e-court as admitted - is formally admitted into evidence. At the same time, there were short portions shown yesterday, Mr. Lukic, but the whole of D1335 is, at this moment, more than two hours, and you're invited to see whether you can reduce the size and focus on the portions that were played in court. Could we hear from you in, well, let's say, within one week approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we make it one week. Then, finally, since Mr. Mladic is not present, we'll have sessions of one hour and a half. That's three such sessions separated by two breaks of half an hour. And, Mr. Lukic, you're expected, in view of the time you've taken until now, to finish in the first session. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for your information, Mr. Mladic has waived his right to be present today so we'll proceed in his absence. I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D05499 on our screens. We need page 204 in the B/C/S and the same page in the English version. While we're waiting for the document to appear, I wanted to inform the Chamber that there is an error in the existing translation into English. It concerns the numbering of paragraphs. It seems that photograph 150 has been switched for a paragraph number, resulting in paragraphs 190 to 198 being different in the two versions between the English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you check if we have the right pages on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously not, Your Honour. Thank you. I do have in B/C/S version, and I need paragraph 193 in English version. That's the ... in these eight paragraphs there is a difference by one. So I -- we need the next page in English version. There we go. So paragraph 192 in B/C/S corresponds to paragraph 193 in English version. And since -- I don't know whether we would be able to correct the translation since we got it in PDF from -- but we'll try to correct that since we have to make some other corrections and we'll try to sort that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it would help that if everyone who has to work with it has a copy where it clearly is indicated what has been changed so that we have working material so that we don't have to reconstruct all the corrections which were made on the original one. And as I suggested yesterday, and I think you followed that suggestion, you can also include the wrong numbering of ... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will discuss incident F-12 of 18 November 1994. It is stated that fire was opened on Dzenana Sokolovic and her son Nermin while they were walking along Zmaja od Bosne Street. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was characteristic of this case, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, Dzenana Sokolovic walked along the street with her son Nermin and her daughter, moving from the settlement of Hrasno towards a house in Bistrik, towards the east. She was also carrying some firewood. At some point, a bullet hit her, passing through her abdomen and hitting her son in the head where he was killed. She was transferred to a hospital and, luckily enough, survived. The basic problem was to determine from which side Dzenana Sokolovic was hit, since there were many contradictions in terms of her entry wound. In her medical documentation it is stated that she was hit from left to right; whereas the police reports and according to her own statement it was the other way around. Therefore, that was the most difficult thing to determine: From which direction the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next I'd like to have 1D05602. We need page 2 in both versions. We'll focus our attention on paragraph 9. This is Dzenana Sokolovic's statement where she says that: "On this particular day, as far as I could remember, it was the 18th of November, 1994. The time could have been around 11.00 a.m., and a cease-fire was in force. I was" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have both B/C/S on the screen. Can we have English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have it by now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "I was returning from my mother-in-law in Hrasno Brdo where I picked up some firewood. I was walking with my two children and it was a bright and sunny day. We were walking towards the centre of town. When we had reached the area closer to the municipal building, I heard shooting going on. All the people on the street started to lay down on the ground. Then suddenly something very hot entered my stomach and I felt severe pain."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we move to next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... suddenly something very hot entered my stomach and I felt severe pain. At the same time, I saw my son fall down. UNPROFOR personnel were present in the vicinity of the shooting. They rushed to the seen, and I was taken to the hospital. In the hospital, I learnt that my son had died on the spot." This is all we wanted to read from the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just ask for clarification. Is it mentioned anywhere else in the statement that the bullet came from the right to the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the direction she described she was moving could help --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where -- where -- but the witness here told us that she said she was struck from the right to the left. I'm looking for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, where did you find that piece of information?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not in this statement. Later on, it came to light in some police reports and her testimony, but it is not in this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, you have presented a report. You should know whether the material this expert relies on in this respect, whether that is in evidence, yes or no. Apparently this statement doesn't help us out. So, therefore, if you want us to seriously consider what the witness said, then make sure that whatever he relies on is before us because, otherwise, we can't ... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Poparic, why is this part of the statement important?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is important because she described the spot where she was hit. It is near the Novo Sarajevo municipal building which is also in Zmaja od Bosne Street. However, it is at some distance from the place in front of the museum where the incident is claimed to have happened by some 1 kilometre away towards the west. So she was moving from Hrasno Brdo towards Marin Dvor where it is asserted she had been hit. The way she describes it, it happened near the municipal building at a distance of 1100 metres. There are also some people mentioned here in this paragraph, whereas later on they are not mentioned later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, again, would you please leave the evaluation of the evidence, even if there's some inconsistencies to the Chamber, and not because whether it's right or wrong what she says here or what she say there is not really within the expertise of a ballistic expert unless he uses it for his weapon and ballistic analysis. If he does so, then what you should do is if there are inconsistent statements, for example, you said: One leads me to these conclusions; however, if I take the other one, it leads me to other conclusions. But it is not for the witness to determine where, who was accurate in testimony, statements, which sometimes we may not even have because they're not in evidence. Would you please keep in mind that this Chamber is finally giving its judgement, whatever it will be, on the basis of the evidence before it and not on the evaluation of the evidence by an expert, evidence which may not be known to us. Please proceed, and I think it's now the third time that I've drawn your attention to this, so therefore please proceed in a focused way, relying on what we'd like to hear; that is, what the expertise of this witness could tell us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Nevertheless I have a question for the witness with respect to the last answer he gave. Page 6, lines 23 and 24 and 25, you say: "The way she describes it, it happened near the municipal building at a distance of 1100 metres." Where can we find this in the statement of the witness, this distance of 1100 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I established the distance because I know where the municipal building is. And I know where the intersection is at which it is claimed she was hit. That is the difference of 1100 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you draw my attention to it in paragraph 9, which was read to you by Mr. Lukic, where she describes it in that way, that you can measure the distance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would need to go back to -- let me try to find in the English version. Now it's gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's back. Please don't touch the screen. In paragraph 9, it was -- I can help you. I can help you. I read --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The fifth line of paragraph 9. She mentions the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the only municipal building she could have passed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: She didn't say anything about the location, the exact location where she was hit. She says, and that was read to you and you should know that: "When we had reached the area closer to the municipal building, I heard shooting going on." It's an area. How can you measure an area and the distance to the building with such a precision of 1100 metres taken from the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I measured the distance from the municipal building to the intersection at Marin Dvor where it is claimed she was hit. She says she was close to the municipal building and I thought it fair because I can't know the exact location. The municipal building is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, the municipal building. Where can we find in this paragraph reference to the intersection at Marin Dvor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She doesn't say it in this paragraph. She just mentions that when she approached the municipal building she could hear shooting and that she was hit. She doesn't say in the paragraph that she was hit at Marin Dvor but close to the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now I understand that you were measuring an area which is not described in this paragraph and the distance of the area to the -- to a building and specifically saying 1100 metres. Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I also --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to the translation problem. Maybe it will solve a lot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's a translation problem, you are in a position to try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- resolve it, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S version, probably the version that was read to this lady, it says "close to the municipal building," not "close to the area of municipal building."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In English it says "closer to the area of the municipal building" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S it says -- I'll read in B/C/S: [Interpretation] "When we approached the municipal building ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's not close to the municipal building. That is approaching, that is, coming closer to. I do understand that there may be a translation issue, but at the same time coming closer to a building is not something you could take as a starting point for measuring a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only if it is translated "coming closer," I would translate it "when we come close to the municipal building." That is what it says in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The translation into B/C/S will have do be verified in this case. That's what should be done, and we'll be better able to assess what problem there is, if there's any. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question to ask, so ... Sir, at page 6, lines 23, where Judge Fluegge referred you to, you said that it happened near the municipal building at a distance of 1100 metres. And at page 8, you say: "I know where the intersection is at which it is claimed she was hit." Now, you say she was hit in the intersection in page 8. In 6, you say, it was -- it happened near the municipal building at a distance of 1100 metres. Now you have just explained that the distance of 1100 metres is the distance between where happened and the intersection; but in paragraph 8, you say then it happened at the intersection. Which is which?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's obviously a misunderstanding. According to the indictment and according to the police reports she was hit at the intersection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me -- let me stop you there. I'm just asking you to explain the two versions that you have given now. I'm not talking about the indictment. Unless you're saying you were misinterpreted here or misrecorded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not mention two versions. I mentioned the intersection at which I know she was hit. It is at Marin Dvor, between the museum and the school of philology. The municipal building is 1100 metres away from the intersection. I measured the distance between the municipal building to the intersection in order to give an impression of the distance. She said: I was approaching the municipal building. The municipal building is 1100 metres away from the intersection. That's all. In this statement she said she was near the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. But I'm saying in paragraph 8 [sic] you then say: "And I know where the intersection is at which it is claimed she was hit." Now are you saying it is claimed that she was hit at the intersection, not at the building. That's the difference that I'm trying to resolve here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, when I said that, I had in mind the intersection specified in the indictment as the place where she was hit. It is between the museum and the school of philology. That intersection is quite removed from the place where ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens, please, P951.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a police report about that incident. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what does it say in the report? Where was she hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that she was hit at the intersection of the Franjo Racki and Zmaja od Bosne Street, which is between the museum and the Faculty of Philosophy. That is that intersection that I mentioned earlier that I am familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you refer us in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what the witness has before him, is that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have it. Please put your questions to the witness, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're just going to briefly deal with the injuries now. We need to look at page 7 in the English version and page 11 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see here at the bottom of the page which it says that the entry point of the wound is visible, 0.5 centimetres wide. It's very faint.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness, please adjust the microphone if you speak because if you are leaned over to the screen, the interpreters cannot hear you. So please take care what you want to say reaches us. Well, mainly -- okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- can you please repeat what you said a second ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just tried to assist Mr. Lukic because on my screen, the visibility is better. 0.5 centimetres and the wound is bleeding, and the exit wound is visible to the paramedian right, 3 times 2 centimetres, and also bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we've read. Now, please, a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So from which side was Dzenana Sokolovic hit according to the medical report?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the medical report, she was hit from the left side and the exit wound is on the right side. And the description of the wounds and the size of it corresponds to the size of the entry and the exit wound because the exit wound is always smaller than the entry wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And according to this report, from which side was the boy, Nermin Divovic, hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the report, the boy, Nermin, was hit from the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's also look at the official report. Page 4 in the English version and -- page 4 in the B/C/S version and page 5 in the English version. [In English] Sorry, B/C/S 5; English 4. [Interpretation] This is the last paragraph on this page in the B/C/S version and the last-but-one in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we can see there that the entry wound was on the right side, the exit wound was on the left side of the stomach. The son of Dzenana Sokolovic, Nermin Divovic, aged 7, succumbed to his wounds on the way to hospital. The entry wound was at the back of the head above the right ear and the exit wound on the face, below the left eye.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this, it was on the right-hand side. However, the description of the wound does not correspond to the actual situation that we can see on the photograph of the boy. One wound was below the right eye and the other wound is above the left ear. The description given here by the police does not correspond to the actual sustained injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is in evidence and it can be looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at a video, please. That's 1D05924, please. We need to look at the timer, 1 hour, 17 minutes, 23 seconds to 1 hour, 17 minutes, 26 seconds. So we just need to look at the three seconds of the footage. But before we begin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the number for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 65 ter or timing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person in the footage, Mr. Poparic?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Mrs. Dzenana Sokolovic on this footage, and the recording was made in the hospital and it was broadcast on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What should we pay attention to when we look at the footage?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need to look at the places where the bandages are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need to look at the stomach?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we play those 3 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You viewed this footage. What did you see?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've let this go now for a very long time, but it strikes me we're getting into an area of forensic pathology or medical expertise, and we haven't heard any evidence from this witness whatsoever that -- to show that he has any background in either of those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us hear what Mr. Poparic has to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, there's an objection against the kind of questions you're asking him. So then that's not resolved by saying "let's hear what he says."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We think it is important to establish the wounds as well if you want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the issue is whether that should be done by a doctor or by a weapon and ballistic expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It should be done by a doctor, if we want to have it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to have it, if you want to present it, then call a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he cannot answer what we all see here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What he can do is, and we're not then looking at this, is say: Well, starting from this assumption, and he may have taken that from wherever he wants it, starting from an assumption that this or this was the case. And then, of course, later you'll have to -- we will have to establish whether that assumption is a right assumption or a wrong assumption, and then can he draw any conclusions on ballistics. But it's not for this witness to establish and it's not the first time, I think I repeated this several, several, several times, it's not for this witness to evaluate on the basis of evidence - which is not footnoted, by the way - often saying a first statement, second statement, this must be right, that must be -- let's try to stick this witness to where his expertise lies. So if the witness came to any conclusion, then we'll hear what -- on what that is based, on what assumption, but not for him to establish the details of what seems to be in the field of forensic pathology. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to draw your attention that it's in his report. It was at figures 153. And we would offer this video into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Well, if he in his report draws conclusions, that's not different from what he does in court, Mr. Lukic. So, therefore, if you think to circumvent it by just pointing to his report, then I'm afraid that you may be disappointed. And -- but if you say it's in this and this paragraph, then we'll carefully look at it, whether there's any proper basis for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it's paragraph 199. We would just offer this video, this clip into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On -- for what purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So everybody can see the wounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there's a suggestion that we could see any relevant thing on this video. Therefore, the Chamber decided we'll look at it. You played the portion you wanted to. If we see anything which, without further explanation, would assist us, we may decide to admit it. If, however, we do not see anything, then you should call someone who could explain to us what is there to be seen relevant which gives the video then probative value. And before we could that, have you ever met Ms. Sokolovic, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know her personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether this is Ms. Sokolovic, I take it that it is her, but you couldn't tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm it because it's a -- it's footage that was broadcast on television. There is a report. I don't know if it's there, in the footage. It was broadcast in the news programme and they said that was Mrs. Sokolovic, so that's how I know. So if the television referred to her correctly, then it is Mrs. Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's exactly what I wanted to point out. If the television is right, it's Ms. Sokolovic. If the television is wrong, it's not Ms. Sokolovic. You just don't know, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know it personally, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, play the portion you want to play. We'll then see --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask Mr. Poparic whether he knows this lady standing next to Barry Hogan and giving her statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he has never met her so the same story is true. If Mr. Hogan is right, the witness is right -- I'm not saying that we have serious --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If Mr. Hogan is not right, we will accept it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you can play the portion of the video and we'll then decide whether or not it has, at this moment, such probative value that we can admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or was it just the seconds we have looked at?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are trying to see if there's introduction, yeah. Can we hear it with the sound now? Maybe a bit longer so we might hear the name. Can we start from the same point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if this is what you tender, Mr. Lukic, then the admission is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, did you see Dzenana Sokolovic talking to the Barry Hogan in the video footage?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you measure how tall Mrs. Sokolovic was in relation to Barry Hogan; and did you know how tall he was?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't measure it, but I did make an estimate because there was no information about how tall Mrs. Sokolovic was and how tall her son was. And this is actually quite important information in order to be able to evaluate if this bullet actually hit both Dzenana Sokolovic and her son. This is particularly important when determining the side from which the shot came. I tried to assess the height of Dzenana Sokolovic because I did have some footage where she was talking to Barry Hogan, and on the basis of his height, I made an assessment or a statement of her height.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How tall is Mr. Barry Hogan?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Barry Hogan is 1 metre .93 centimetres tall, but I made an estimate with a kind of reserve. I took it as being 1 metre .95, because it's an estimate. We can't be precise. And I came to the conclusion that Mr. Dzenana Sokolovic was 1.65 centimetres [as interpreted] tall, and there could be a small margin of error. She could have been taller, but in my estimate she could not have been taller than 1.65 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, where do you get it from that Mr. Barry Hogan is 1 metre 93?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the -- at the beginning, when I worked in the Karadzic case, I didn't know how tall he was. So I was forced to make an evaluation. And before I testified, I actually asked Mr. Hogan how tall he was and he told me 1.93 metres. I did make that estimate, but I rounded it up, and I mentioned why I did that and actually that turned out to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Finally you answered my question. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we have it on the transcript, Your Honour: I asked Mr. Barry Hogan how tall he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who asked, you or the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's why I say he has finally answered my question. All what he was saying before in trying to answer my question was irrelevant to my question. When he says "I asked Barry Hogan," now he was answering my question and that was what I was telling him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is your conclusion in this case? Could they have been hit with the same bullet; and what would be the difference in the height between the boy's head and the mother's stomach?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't have any information about the height of the boy. I couldn't find that anywhere. But in the photograph of the boy lying at the cross-roads, an estimate can be made because there is an area in the intersection, which I measured myself, that was the standard in the former Yugoslavia, it's 50 centimetres wide. And on the basis of that, I estimated that he could have been 1.20 metres tall, or 1.10. Why is this important? If the boy was next to the mother, it's important to see whether the wound in his head was at the level of the stomach wound of Mrs. Sokolovic. According to the footage that we just looked at, in my estimate, and I did consult -- I'm not a forensic pathologist, but I did consult with a professor of forensic medicine who died, unfortunately, a few days ago --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. This Chamber is not interested in hearsay pathological expertise from other persons. If we need that, either Mr. Lukic or the Prosecution will call such experts. But second-hand hearsay of such expertise is not what we expect from this -- from you as a witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my assessment, Dzenana Sokolovic, as far as I am versed in these things, was hit a little bit below the belly button. On the basis of that and in view of her height, I concluded that these two wounds - in the head of the boy and her stomach - are not overlapping if the shot came from the right side. If the shot came from the left side, then it's possible for those wounds to line up. If they were next to each other. But if it came from the right side, since that is the estimate, if they were far apart, and the further apart they were, the lower would be the point of the wound of the second person. So I have given you an explanation of the basis for my conclusions. The boy could not have been struck with the same bullet if it had come from the right side. If it had come from the left side, there was a possibility that they were both struck with the same bullet. That is my assessment in view of all the shortcomings in the documents. Unfortunately, the forensic analysis in these cases would be of crucial importance, and, unfortunately, we don't have it. It would have been very useful to have measured the height of the wound of Mrs. Dzenana Sokolovic, and, unfortunately, I was not in a position to make that measurement. Then we would have reached the most precise measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you talk about the left and the right side, whose positions are on what side? If it was one bullet, from which side could it have come?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had come from the right side, then the assumption was that it was fired from the Metalka building because it is in that area. And then that would have been from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. On the left-hand side, however, everything was under the control of the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if the bullet had come from the right side, could it have caused both wounds, from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of all of these assumptions, which I had to have used, that could not have been the case. So I repeat again that the most proper way to have done it would have been to measure the entry and exit wounds of Mrs. Sokolovic. That would have been very useful in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I would now like to move to incident F-14 from your document 1D05499.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S version, it begins on page 218; and in the English version, it begins on page 209 -- no, actually, 226. I apologise. It would be item 209. That on 23rd of November, 1994, a tram was hit in the street Zmaja od Bosne between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks, and at that time two persons were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, in the meantime, can we look at 1D00691.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are looking at a statement of Huso Palo. And in both versions, we're looking at paragraph -- that's immediately below the statement, the words -- the word "statement." That paragraph states that Mr. Huso Palo stated the following: "On 23rd of November, 1994, I was driving tram garage number 263. At 1535 hours I was heading towards -- from Marin Dvor towards Remiza, and when I reached the section between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a translation error there, Mr. Lukic? It says in the English: I reached the -- "I was heading towards Marin Dvor and Remiza ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From Marin Dvor towards Remiza.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what the English says but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters confirm that there is an error in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we proceed on the basis of there being an error so we understand this and it should be further then -- we would receive a new translation. For the time being we start from -- reading it as "from Marin Dvor to Remiza." Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "And when I reached the section between the technical school and the Marsal Tito barracks, specifically the turning that splits off towards the new railway station, I heard a sound of something hitting the tram, as if someone had thrown a stone at me. The passengers reacted, shouting to hurry up because someone in the tram had been wounded. I drove on to the first stop where the traffic police were located and stopped there."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you draw any conclusions as to where was the place where the tram was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This piece of information is very important. There are two versions of events. According to one witness, Afeza Karadzic asserted that the tram was hit at the intersection of Franje Racki. That is the previous intersection between the museum and the Faculty of Philosophy. But here we see that the driver, Huso Palo, said that this was at the place where the turning was, and in my assessment this is 50 metres forward towards the west. Another witness who was wounded in this incident, Sabina Sabanic I think is her name, yes, Sabina Sabanic, she described the event slightly differently but it corresponds to this. She said that she heard a shot. People started screaming. The tram continued a little bit further and stopped near the Marsal Tito barracks, which more or less comports with what Huso Palo said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I've been spending some time, since the witness has mentioned some names of his -- the witnesses who are sources of information for what he is saying, trying to find out if these specific statements he refers to are evidence before this Chamber. And they're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It will be. I will tender 1D691 now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are what? They are evidence now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is 1D00691 and I want to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This one in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness -- and you may not have understood Ms. Edgerton well. I think the witness referred to other statements which would be inconsistent with this one or consistent or, I mean, whatever. And I think Ms. Edgerton said that what the witness refers to, apart from what we now read in the statement, that that's not in evidence. Is it, Mr. Lukic, or is it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not. Then the comment of this witness on this document loses much of its probative value, I would say, because he refers to matters which we are unable to verify. Unless we have it clearly in his statement, precise sources, and if you are still about to tender those sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will tender this document, Your Honour, for the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we will mark this document for identification pending verification of the translation because there was -- there were even more differences with what was read to us. That has no consequences that part of the comment of the witness to other references are unclear to the Chamber. We don't know what it is about. So, therefore, we just look at what this witness has given us, a statement. And if you want us to in any way establish something about consistency with other statements, then what the witness has told is not a sufficient basis for that. Because we don't know what it is, we don't know whether it's in evidence. Madam Registrar, the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1336, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification pending translation verification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise when I mentioned witness Sabanic in my report, it is stated that it is P01913 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one asked you -- no one asked you any question at this moment. It's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's appreciated. It's appreciated that you want to assist us, but no one asked you. Mr. Lukic will deal with the matter, or Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, it is P1915 where we can find this statement of Ms. Sabina Sabanic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And not therefore P1913 as the witness said a second ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, also P1913.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there are various statements --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And P1914.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have three statements and it's for the Chamber to check what we should make out of that. Okay. If that's what you wish us to do, please proceed meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, what is your conclusion? Where was the tram hit from and where could it not have been hit from?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, given the contradictory statements about the location of the tram, I considered both variants: That it was hit at the place asserted by Witness Karadzic, which is at the intersection between the museum and the school of philosophy, and the other variant, that it was hit close to the technical school, close to where the tram tracks fork. If the tram was hit at the intersection between the museum and the school of philosophy, it could not have been targeted from the white high-rise buildings. If it was at the other location, then it could not have been targeted from the Metalka building but it could have been targeted from the white high-rises in Grbavica. That is the basic difference. The basic conclusion is that in neither of the cases, the tram was hit neither from the Metalka building nor from the white high-rises, irrespective of where it was. I reached that conclusion based on facts. In particular, the fact that the two women were wounded and on the basis of their wounds. First of all, the police asserted that they were wounded by one bullet which, when impacting the glass pane, shattered, which is impossible. But when the tram stopped, they found a shattered pane where the women were injured and their conclusion was that it was the only way that the bullet had come through, falling apart and hitting them both. My conclusion is, given their position and their detailed explanations and given the description of their wounds, that they could only have been hit if the bullet came through the joint of the articulated tram, the soft part, but in that case, it would have had to have been from the building of the Executive Council of Bosnia-Herzegovina and not from the Metalka or the white high-rises, irrespective of the tram's location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have much time left so I -- we need to go back to 1D05499; it is your report. I wanted to ask you something about F-17 of the 6th of March, 1995, in Sedrenik Street --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The report is now D1330.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So D1330. Tarik Zunic was hid in Sedrenik on his way back from school in that particular incident. We need photograph 183 in your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English it is page 249; in the B/C/S 242.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell us what can be seen in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the place of incident, marked with the red ellipsis, viewed from Spicasta Stijena. I took the photograph. The buildings are small, but one could make out two specific buildings with white roofs that are almost identical, and it was important in order to pin-point the place of incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the weapon that wounded Tarik Zunic?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statements, it would have been an M84 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Statements?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tarik Zunic's statement. He recognised the sound. Because the M84 has a stronger piercing bullet than a simple rifle, and people could recognise the sound produced by the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at 1D05628 next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just for your information, I wasn't able to see on that photograph two buildings with white roofs, but I leave it to that. If you have seen them, please be aware that I didn't see them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We need page 2 in both versions from this statement of Tarik Zunic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is his statement of 10 November 1995. The third paragraph in both versions. It says: "On the day I was injured, I was wearing jeans and a green jacket. It was cloudy but without fog. Spicasta Stijena was on my left side at that moment. Having passed along this canvas protection I heard two shots. I recognised immediately that the shots were fired by an M84 machine-gun. The sound is louder than the sound of ordinary rifles. I can easily tell the difference because I had heard so many shots that it is now possible for me to make this distinction." That was it regarding the type of weapon, but how were you able to establish the place where he was hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to Tarik Zunic's statement, the incident took place near a building with a double-slanted roof as can be seen --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the number of photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He marked the place --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Stop. The interpreters did not hear the number.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 241, image 181 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who took photograph 181?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was marked by Tarik Zunic. We visited that location, stopping at the shop to inspect the site. However, the other building is almost identical. There were some people there, and one of them called us and told us it wasn't there, it was this way. They asserted he had been wounded next to a pole that can be seen. Perhaps some 2 or 3 metres to the right from it. They said he had been wounded there, and the person in question claimed that he had helped him.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a bit of patience. We'll come there. Just a bit of patience, we'll come to the transcript --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I just want to -- I just want to have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. -- one second --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now you'll get it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She is just taking my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: She has right to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have much time left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Ms. Edgerton intervenes or wishes to object, she has an opportunity to do so. And before you think you could refer to her possibility to deal with the matter in cross-examination, we should first hear what she wants to say. And that's what I'm going to do now, what the Chamber's going to do now, hear what the objection is by Ms. Edgerton. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I actually only wanted to ask if we could just have a look at the page where image 181 is in e-court so that we could see what the witness was talking about. That was absolutely all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is perfectly right. Mr. Lukic, tell us what page in the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the Prosecution would tell me how do I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- conduct my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic. Last warning. Last warning or we'll ask co-counsel to take over. Because what you are doing is totally inappropriate. You can tell us now at what page we'll find the photograph the witness testifies about and then we'll look at it so that we are able to follow the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One observation on my part, Mr. Lukic. You asked the witness who took photograph 181. This question is not answered. Instead of answering that simple question, you let him go ten lines with other explanation. This is consuming of your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let's go back to the photograph. Photograph 181 is found on page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 248 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And 241 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said 248 in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a look at that and meanwhile you may continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's upper image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, do you know who took the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. In any case, it was marked by Tarik Zunic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where and when?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he testified in the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 1D05629 on our screens now, please. That's the testimony of Tarik Zunic on 7th February 2007, and we need page 24 in e-court that would -- should correspond to transcript page 1725. We need rows, or lines, 2 to 8. Mr. Zunic was asked: "Q. Were you carrying anything at that time? "A. Yes. I had a blue rucksack with my schoolbooks and other things on my right shoulder. "Q. Could I ask you right now to stand up and show the Court how you were carrying the rucksack at the time you were shot. "A. I carried it over my right shoulder and I was holding it with my right hand. Is this all right?"

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was Tarik Zunic hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the medical documentation, he was hit in his right lower arm, and the bullet left his body near the thumb, somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is your conclusion how was he hit?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the statement, actually the testimony, and I wasn't able to view the video, but I analysed all of the possibilities in terms of how he might have carried his rucksack and how a bullet could have arrived from Spicasta Stijena in order to hit him in the lower arm and leave his body near the right thumb. This was the only position that could have happened. Any other position, in my view, would be such that the bullet would have had have come from a different side, from the direction of Sedrenik instead of Spicasta Stijena. On page 243, I illustrated it by providing photograph 184.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which forces were at Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sedrenik was controlled by the Army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one thing. Your whole reconstruction is based on the description the witness gave in his testimony in Milosevic as to how he was positioned and how his rucksack was positioned. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he was walking down the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's different, but I take your "yes" for a confirmation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I offered 1D05628 into evidence. It was the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the portion read? Or let me ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was read, yes, some portion -- one portion is read but it's the whole statement given to the Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that statement, yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D05628 receives Exhibit Number D1337, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would offer part I read from 1D05629 if you deem it necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you read it, and of course a transcript of witness in another case usually is dealt with under Rule 92 bis or 92 ter, but you read the whole portion and I think there was no objection to it being read. And we now know at least what the basis this witness -- was for the witness to further elaborate on what he describes in his report. Please proceed. There's no need, I think, to have it in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would just ask Madam Registrar, with the help of the usher, to provide Mr. Poparic with the exhibit, actually artefact, it's Exhibit P02053, which is the tail-fin. And it's in connection with Markale I.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, can you tell us what kind of shell it is by looking at its tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a 120-millimetre shell with the basic charge being M84.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: M74.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The basic or primary charge of that shell, can be impressed or pushed in?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it has a thread, a groove, that can be used to screw it on and that is the only way to connect it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The last thing you said did not make it into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is delivered with the tail-fin being screwed into the shell. Some other shells, such as M49, of the older type did have different solutions for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the tail-fin being screwed into the shell or are you talking about the primary charge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. The primary charge is screwed into the tail-fin. I can even unscrew it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the question started with the primary charge, and we slowly now moved to the tail-fin being screwed in, which surprised me slightly, but I was seeking confirmation that that is what you said or whether you wanted to say that the primary charge is screwed into the tail-fin, the back end of the tail-fin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it was unclear. The basic or primary charge is screwed in. That is what I was discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You just told us that you could observe that the primary charge can be rotated, just now?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have in your hands the same tail-fin previously?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm afraid there's some misunderstanding. This tail-fin comes from Markale II, whereas I had in my hands the tail-fin from the Markale I incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I confused the numbers. Can the witness be provided with another one, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another one or a specific one, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at it. Yes. Indeed, this one looks more like what we've seen before as related to the Markale I incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you unscrew by hand the primary charge on this one?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you had this tail-fin in your hands previously?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I also took photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, were you able to observe whether the primary charge can be unscrewed from the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where did you examine the tail-fin, this one?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here at the Tribunal on Defence premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was present?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, Aleksandar Stevanovic from Mr. Karadzic's Defence team, and a representative of the Registry who delivered the tail-fin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any tools to unscrew it?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not, and yet we did try to unscrew it but were unsuccessful. I wasn't interested in unscrewing it. It was Mr. Stevanovic who found it interesting, and he was trying to unscrew this end part but couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You worked on constructing different weapons, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to you, is it possible to move the primary charge in relation to the tail-fin?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From my experience, I had scores of tail-fins, not just from this type, but other types which had a similar solution with a thread. It never happened that could you unscrew the tail-fin or is there any force created during explosion that would make it possible to unscrew it. What we have are just axial forces along the axis, and you can see that on photographs of stabilisers from 82-millimetre shells where the primary charge is pushed in, and then during explosions those axial forces sometimes pull out the primary charge or it drops out which indicates that the force that acts upon the tail-fin is axial force. It's not a rotary force. There has to be some kind of rotational force for the primary charge to be unscrewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we are coming close to where we should take a break and you've used, until now, 4 hours and 56 minutes. So you have another -- perhaps we take a little bit of a longer session, you have another ten minutes left, and then we finish. And then after the break, the Prosecution can start its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would continue then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at photographs. Ms. Subotic spoke about the two photographs that you processed and so we will just briefly discuss those.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see 1D0598 [sic], please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 1D05498. In B/C/S, first we need page 46. [Microphone not activated]. Maybe we should have only one version on our screen, for example, English version. It's easier to follow. So we need page 46 in English as well. No, we need the previous ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, this figure 14 we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell us what you did. How did you work on this?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the question was how this photograph was made, what does it show, what was changed in it. I made these comparative photographs. The photograph on the left, which was taken by Roger Richards, was completely untouched. The photograph on the right, which is from the photo file of the police, was changed. Why? What I wanted to do was to show more clearly the position of the craters on the sidewalk in a more clear way so that the difference between the two craters could be seen more easily. There was a problem because the two photographs were taken from different angles, so then I had to take this right-side photograph and I had to reduce the width of the sidewalk to the width of the sidewalk -- I apologise, that you can see on the left-hand photograph. And so there was a small modification there in the way the photograph looks, and I think Judge Fluegge noticed that. This was done in the OmniPage programme. It has that option. By just shifting the grid a little bit you slightly change the perspective of the photograph. In that way, nothing was modified that would affect the drawing of conclusions in this case. The basic idea was to spot the differences between the two craters more easily on the basis of the position in relation to the sidewalk. I think that's obvious. The photograph itself looks a little bit different in the photo file, but the way it looks is closer to the way it actually looked --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last part of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They didn't hear the last part of your previous sentence. So it looked a bit closer to the way it actually looked in relation to what?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to the sidewalk. To the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to the next thing. We don't have time to -- let's look at the next paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, but I want to put one question to the witness, apart from the fact that I didn't deal with the system to change the photograph. What makes you certain that these two photographs depict the same trace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm saying that they show different traces. Because you see on the right-hand photograph the entire crater is greater than the pavement slabs. And here on the left-hand photograph, it's just halfway. So it's obvious that they are different craters. This is what we assert in our report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And -- thank you, Your Honour. And just to move to figure 17 now. It's on page 48 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you process this photograph? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a processed photograph. This is a part of the photograph of Roger Richards. And here, there's an orthogonal projection of the photograph of the crater, so we have lost a part of the picture. That's why we have a blank corner, angle, here. Because when you change the angle of the perspective you lose a part of the photograph. So we have a orthogonal photograph here on the basis of which the conclusion was drawn that the angle of impact was quite large, from 81 to 83 degrees. And in my opinion, this is a very accurate method because the circumstances happen to be such that we knew the size of the pavement slabs and on the basis of that you could determine the size of the crater and so on and so forth. It's pretty accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- Mr. Lukic, yes, I know that you get that one minute extra. Could you tell us what makes you so sure which of the two photographs depicts, if they are different, which of the ones depicts the place of the impact as charged? I mean, which is the one which relates to the -- what happened, the one taken by Mr. - what was his name? - Mr. Roger Richards, or the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is our opinion that the place of impact is shown in the photograph made by Mr. Roger Richards. I will explain why. Because -- and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it is -- well, I don't want to take more time from Mr. Lukic. And I take that we'll find in your report anyhow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have only one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, other than these two photographs, did you alter in any way any other photographs that were in your reports?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not alter the photographs. Sometimes we added something, we drew in lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you change perspectives?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not change perspective in any other photographs. Only in these two photographs that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, thank you very much for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, we'll take a break. You're invited to follow the usher. We take a break a little bit longer. We'll resume at quarter to 12.00. We'd like to see you back then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break of half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Edgerton. You find Ms. Edgerton to your right. Ms. Edgerton is counsel for the Prosecution. Ms. Edgerton, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Poparic.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I want to begin by just getting you to confirm my understanding of your general methodology as you approached the investigation of the range of incidents that are in your report. Some are scheduled, some are unscheduled, some have been dropped, but there's a wide range of them. So, first of all, generally speaking, it's correct, isn't it, that you -- when it came to the location of some Scheduled Incidents, in fact, a number of Scheduled Incidents, you didn't rely on the evidence of the victims, as we saw, for example, yesterday in the film clip relating to F-5, or the witnesses, as we saw yesterday on the film clip relating to F-9. You discounted that evidence; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with that. When we went to the scene, we had in mind all the available documents that we had at that point in time. We did get some later. But, for example, if we're talking about video footage, the recordings made by Barry Hogan, we received those later, once we had done the investigation on the scene. But we did have everything that was available to us at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't find you've answered to my question but we'll come back to those specific incidents and move on on this topic. As part of your methodology, it was also, generally speaking, your practice to discount the results of contemporaneous investigations, like, for example, the UNPROFOR report you referred to in passing yesterday, which is P670 in F -- in relation to F-11. That's the report where, if you'll remember because you mentioned it -- what they did yesterday, the report where they stuck antennas into the furrows in the grass. You discounted the results of contemporaneous investigations like that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. When you mentioned the report, the first time I heard of that report was when I testified in the Karadzic case, and you read an excerpt from that report to me and mentioned the antennas. That was the first time that I heard of them. I didn't even know that there was such a report, which I am sorry about because without it, our job was much more difficult. It would have been much easier had we had that report then.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, can you answer my question? My question was: You discounted that report in your own analysis; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did take it into account in the present analysis. Not in the analysis in the Karadzic case because I didn't have it then. But in the present report, it was -- it was dealt with in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let me try asking you another way. You specifically rejected the results of UNPROFOR's contemporaneous investigation in relation to incident F-11; right? That's what I mean by the word "discounted."

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not agree with some of the parts of that report but I did accept other parts. But I did not completely agree with the conclusions given in the report by UNPROFOR. Even there in the report, there is a report of the 8th and then of the 10th, so there are some inconsistencies in the two reports which were drafted by members of UNPROFOR. My answer is that I did not discount everything, and I did not accept everything. I did accept some things.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm going to try and be as specific as I can in relation to the documents I mention, and I'd like to you confine your answers to those documents, all right? Now, you also, from your reading your report, specifically discounted the work of local investigators; for example, the work that was done in relation to the incident that's labelled F-15 in your report, where you allege that Bosnian investigators doctored a picture. Right? So you specifically -- by making that allegation you specifically reject the contemporaneous local investigation; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite true. I dealt with that in detail and explain why I asserted that. They did draw in a detail and said that that was exit-entrance on the tram, but actually that was incorrect. The exit point was much lower. But it's true, yes, that that's what happened and I gave an explanation of why that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And we'll come back to that too. Also, in terms of your methodology, you didn't go to all the incident locations; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, no. But please let me just refresh my memory, if you think that I am not correct on this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, it's correct, isn't it, that you didn't go, you weren't able to go to the specific incident location for F-1 because it was physically impossible to do so. The site had changed since Mr. Van der Weijden's visit; right? You didn't go to the incident location. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes -- one second. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. Then we have to have the definition of the location. If it's -- he -- this witness didn't go because something changed, does that mean that he didn't go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not an objection in itself. But apparently, Ms. Edgerton, Mr. Lukic has some concerns about going somewhere if the appearance of that location changed. What do you mean exactly? Could you seek to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You weren't able to visit the incident location for Scheduled Incident F-1 because it simply no longer existed; correct? The site had been changed. The house had been changed. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The house had changed. I explain that here. A room was attached, built in front of the front door. I don't know if Mr. Van der Weijden was there so it was impossible to get to that place. But the photograph that I made together with Mr. Van der Weijden is quite --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the photograph. I want to go on because you asked me to be a little bit more precise to some of the other incident locations that you couldn't visit. It's correct, isn't it, because you confirmed it in your testimony in the Karadzic case, that you also didn't visit the incident location in respect of incident F-2 in your report?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: F-2 ... excuse me. Allow me just to refresh my memory about that. I don't know if I went by dates here. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You can find it at paragraph 37 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, clear. I found it. I was in front of that house, and I explained that at the time I was not at the actual location because it's been changed. (redacted) (redacted) so I thought that I shouldn't be going there anyway. But the location was changed, yes, like in the previous instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for a moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
