utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you also didn't visit the location of the Unscheduled Incident with the date of 22 November 1994, which is referred to at English page 255 and B/C/S page 249 of your report; right? You didn't go there. You made your analysis on the basis of videos and photographs.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just give me a moment, please. I just want to remind myself what exactly that is. 22nd of November, 1994. 249. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It starts at paragraph 253.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes -- no, I was there. I was in that street. Rogina Street. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to the specific incident location for the incident you describe as number 9 from 15 May 1995 in your Annex 6, paragraph 41?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Perhaps you can assist me by describing it. It would make it easier for me than to go by paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we can follow as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 40? Maybe I'll find it. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's the incident of -- can I just repeat it for my friend Mr. Lukic. It's the incident of small-arms fire in Djordja Andrejevica Kuna Street number 7 on 15 May 1995. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the page number? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The English page number is 346. It's paragraph 41, incident 9 in Annex 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness has B/C/S version in front of him. Can you provide us with B/C/S page number?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think he's found it, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you found it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have. I can respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I visited the location. If you have in mind the apartment itself, I didn't go into the apartment. But I lived in a neighbouring building in an apartment that looked exactly like that because they are all of the same type. I am fully aware of both the location and the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Okay. But however aware you might be, the fact is, you weren't -- you didn't go to the specific, the physical -- you didn't physically go to the specific incident location for your Unscheduled Incident 9. You weren't in the apartment; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, this question is answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not physically. I did not go there physically.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you also didn't go to the specific incident location of your Unscheduled Incident number 10 -- or pardon me, the Unscheduled Incident of 10 December 1994, which is at English page 259 and B/C/S page 253; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one moment. I need to jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You did your --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct that I wasn't at that particular place but I did visit the location. I didn't go to the exact spot, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Just one further question, then, with respect to that incident. So you never went, if I understand you correctly, you never went to the exact GPS co-ordinates that were identified in relation to that incident at all; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go to the place of the co-ordinates, but I did visit the area and I saw the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, just on the subject of GPS co-ordinates, it's correct that in going to the locations that you did visit, you didn't use a GPS at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not use it because there was no need.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So, in fact, you completely discounted the GPS co-ordinates for any of these incidents for the incident locations as well as the assessed origins of fire, even though you had those co-ordinates available to you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The co-ordinates were provided only by Mr. Van der Weijden, if I remember well. There are some mentioned in certain UNPROFOR reports, but more when it comes to shelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was not who gave those co-ordinates but whether you ignored them. That was the question. Could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that I did not rely on them because they were not necessary for my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And if I can just remind you of what you said in the Karadzic case, and if you would like we can display the transcript so you can read it, in fact what you said about GPS -- having a GPS system was that you didn't see a reason to use one because having a GPS system wouldn't have made a big difference. And that's at Karadzic transcript page 39181, lines 2 to 12. So let us know if you'd like to see it. I could show it to you. But, if not, tell me if you agree or stand by the evidence you gave previously?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No need, thank you. I think I've answered already and I stand by it. And I can explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask a question in this respect. You emphasised various times during the examination-in-chief how important it was to know exactly where -- where incidents took place, what the location was, and you are now telling us that you didn't need GPS for that, which is a relatively objective and also a relatively - but correct me when I'm wrong - a relatively accurate way of defining a certain location.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolutely right. But in this case, I did not have reliable information about GPS co-ordinates so as to say the shooter was at this or that co-ordinate. If I had had such information, it would have been important for me to find it. But I did not have it. Therefore, I can measure all you like but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we're not only talking about location of shooters, I think, but - please correct me when I'm wrong, Ms. Edgerton - we're also talking about locations where people who were hit by bullets were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Indeed, my specific examples in relation to the victims, the first questions related to F-5 and F-16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were mainly focusing --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Which is where the victims -- or about where the victims were found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, could you please then answer my question as well, why GPS doesn't assist in any way if it comes to the locations where victims said they had been or where they have been reported to have been when they were struck by bullet fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll answer that. There were only a few cases where we know exactly where the victims were. For example, the case under the bridge, I don't know what incident number it is exactly. But there we have a clear description, so that location is fully known and defined. The edge of the river. All tram sites were defined by the rails, whether they were straight or bent, and what intersection between the museum and the school of philosophy. So there are several locations that in and of themselves are sufficiently defined and co-ordinates wouldn't help. On the other hand, I don't know the co-ordinates of the shooters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about F-5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me remind myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mother and daughter, where you drew all kind of conclusions on the basis of one step taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. I mean F-4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is fully defined, F-4. It was fully defined. It's known exactly. The pavement. No mistake there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I can get clarification. Sir, you keep referring to not having co-ordinates of the shooter. Was the exercise that you were undertaking not, in fact, supposed to determine where the shooter might have been given the other information? In other words, if we had known where the shooter was, the whole exercise would be futile. There's no need for the exercise. Then we just say, There's the shooter. So why do you expect, then, that you should have had co-ordinates for the shooter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to answer although I'm not certain I understand. It is very important to know where the source of fire was but we didn't have that information. In my analysis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that's the purpose of the investigation. That's the purpose of the investigation. So you can't investigate that which you already -- let me, sir. You can't investigate that which you already know. If you have the co-ordinate of the shooter, then there is no need for the investigation. The investigation is being undertaken to determine precisely who -- where the -- first the direction and then possibly to find out where the shooter might have been. That's the purpose of the investigation. Therefore you cannot have, in advance, co-ordinates of the shooter. Can you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not complaining about not having received co-ordinates, but I'm just saying that if I had used a GPS device it would not have been of much help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You are not answering my question. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And just talking about the locations of the shooter, to go back to locations that you didn't visit, it's correct, isn't it, that you haven't been anywhere in any of the white sky-scrapers that are the alleged origins of fire for a number of tram sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I did not go to the sky-scrapers, but I did accept the position that there were sniping positions there and I am fully cognizant of their co-ordinates as well as their direction. I even have photographs from the sky-scrapers where one can see what the visibility was of particular areas. I think I had sufficient information to assess ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Mr. Poparic, we'll come to that too. In terms of other assessed origins of fire that you didn't visit, it's also correct that you have never been inside the school for the blind; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was next to the school for the blind several times. I wasn't inside the building itself. It was reconstructed in the meantime. There wasn't much for me to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, just to move on in terms of your site visits, because you've made more than one, in fact you've made several, it sounds like, you were taken to locations by a local who, among other things, had been a member of a tank crew in the SRK; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, in terms of your professional background, it's correct that you have no formal training in criminal investigation whatsoever; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No formal training -- you also have no formal training in forensic pathology; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You're not a doctor; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And as you said yesterday, you're not a lawyer. You confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You've never been a judge?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You have no formal legal training; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formal? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Does that mean that you're confirming my question: Have you had formally legal training, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to answer that. I do have a certain level of education and training, but I don't know what level is of interest. It is difficult for me to answer precisely. I'm not someone who has absolutely no legal knowledge, but I can't define what level of legal knowledge that would be.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Have you ever been to law school?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And it's also correct, isn't it, that you have no experience in geographical survey; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do have some kind of military professional training because we were doing something in terms of surveying, but let's say I don't have it. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I want to talk a little bit now about the map that you refer to in your report and that you took cutouts from in your report. And those appear at pages 56, 104, and 127 in English, and 59, 105, and 125 in your language. And you also mentioned the map in your testimony yesterday at transcript pages 40448, 40473 to -74, and 40487. Now, it's correct, isn't it, that that map has an operative date of March 1st to 14 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, you don't say that anywhere in your report, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was stated so, but the reference is there to the map. I don't know whether the dates are mentioned though.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'd like you to go have a look at page 59 and tell me whether you see the operative date of the map that you've just confirmed there.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a part of the map, since it's a large map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can't be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it 59 in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And 56 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct. Correct. And, for the record, that's -- that -- this cutout is taken from Exhibit P2952, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So you don't see anywhere on this page reference -- you don't point out anywhere on this page that you're using a map from 1995, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can't be seen in this cutout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we see the footnote in the English version. I think there's a reference, footnote 44 in relation to image 27: "The image is part of the operations map of the commander of the BH army's 12th Division."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it doesn't give the dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Correct. There's no reference to date which is what the focus of my question is about, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I understood this.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And, in fact, nowhere in your report do you point out that you're using a map from 1995 as evidence of the positions of the front line in relation to an incident in September 1994 in Hrasno, that's F-4; and November 1993 in Brijesce Brdo, that's F-5. So you haven't told us within the 300-plus pages of your report that the map you're using to illustrate the front lines isn't even from -- as of the date of these incidents, isn't even from the year in which the incidents happened; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree. There's a reference for the map and on the map can you see it in big letters, if you show it. You can see the dates for the map. I may have referenced the date, but I don't think it's a major error. I didn't hide anything. Whoever wanted to look at the integral map would see it for themselves. There's nothing secret about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I directly ask the question to you. You are you using these extracts of these maps to support your conclusions about an event which took place at a certain date. Those maps are not valid for that date. Do you consider that you should have drawn our attention to the fact that this portion of the underlying information you used may be inaccurate because it refers -- it's not related to the same date? Or do you consider it, as an expert witness, better to say: Well, if you want to find out this discrepancy, go to the original map, look at the dates, and then you'll find what I at least have not explicitly stated in my report? Which of the two do you think would be appropriate? You drawing our attention to it or we doing the puzzle journey and try to find out that there is some discrepancy of which we do not know yet how important or how unimportant it is? Which of the two do you think would be appropriate to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation], of course, it would be more appropriate for me to mention it, but I'll explain why I didn't. The map was used so many times, and by inertia, I just referenced it without specifying the date. It was no intention on my part to hide anything. You are correct, it would have been more appropriate to have stated a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Should you have used it at all, if it's not applicable for the time of the incident, to draw any conclusions on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I gave it some thought, but I had many other documents specifying in which parts the separation lines did not change. In the Sarajevo theatre, since it was very specific, there were very few changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you drew conclusions without specifying why you drew that conclusion. I'm not saying whether they are right or wrong, but you considered it not necessary to explain to us that although the map is wrong, at least is not applicable for that date, that for other reasons you think it is still reliable enough to use. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true I did not do that, but in most cases I did say that I visited the locations and that it was my assessment that it tallied. Specifically, for example, F-4, where the mother and child were, I told you I was there, and I told you that the set-up of the area was such so as to confirm what we see on the map. In many other cases, as can be seen in these photographs here, I visited --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I interrupt you there. We are exclusively talking about maps with separation lines. Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You just mentioned F-4. And in relation to this same map, I want to jump over to that incident for a minute, and you can find it beginning at page 100 in your language of your report, and that covers paragraphs 64 to 79. And, in English, it begins at page 97. And in relation to this map, I want to draw your attention specifically to your image 73. All right? That's at English page 104. So you used this map that you've got the cutout of here and you confirmed it yesterday. You used markings on this map to establish that the closest VRS position could have been at around 680 metres from the spot where the two victims were shot. And that was at transcript page 40448, lines 11 to 12. And you said that you either couldn't determine visibility of the incident site, at transcript page 40448, or that there was no line of sight from this position 680 metres away, and that was at 40473. Now, the basis -- it's correct, isn't it, that the basis for your determination of the position of the front lines is a pencil mark on this map; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which line do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The lawyer is talking of a mark, not a line.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Look at your paragraph 70. You said the separation line along this stretch of Ozrenska Street shifted towards Ivana Krndelja Street by about 100 metres, image 73, meaning that the closest positions of the Army of the Republika Srpska could have been around 680 metres from the spot where the two victims were shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we please be shown paragraph 70. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, in the Karadzic case, during your testimony there, you confirmed that the basis for the statement that I've just read out is a pencil mark that you found on the map. And if you would like to see that reference, we can have a look at it. It's at Karadzic transcript page 39229, and it's 65 ter number 32790, e-court page 67, but let us know if you need to see it.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which one you mean. There are two lines here, drawn in markers. I don't know which pen you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's go over to the Karadzic transcript, please, if we could. As I mentioned 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you direct the witness to what you mean by pencil marking.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Oh --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I couldn't see it in this version of his report. It's only visible in the Karadzic version of his report so I would like to get him to have a look at his assertions in the Karadzic case at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I suggest is that we have the Karadzic transcript on the right-hand side and that we keep on the left-hand side the map so that can you read from the transcript and that we could, at the same time, have a look at the map. If at least you have a 65 ter number for the upload of the Karadzic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: 32790, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that we do not have a document under that number. Let's have a look at your ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been released now, I understand. So could we have a look at on the one side of the screen the Karadzic transcript, and you indicate what page, Ms. Edgerton, and then we keep the map on the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In your list of documents to be used, it is indicated that it is under seal. But this part is in open session, and, therefore, there may be no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So at lines -- I'll actually read to you lines -- you can read English a little bit also, I think, Mr. Poparic, can't you? But I'll read to you --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'll read to you lines 1 to 8 so it can be translated and then perfectly clear. In Karadzic, I asked you: "Q. Mr. Poparic, I'd like to move on to another incident now and it's incident F-4, that's the first one that you spoke about in your examination-in-chief, and it's at paragraphs 53 to 61 of your report. And just a couple of brief questions. In paragraph 59, when you say that the line shifted towards Ivana Krndelja Street by about 100 metres, your basis for that is the pencil mark on the cutout of the 1995 dated map we discussed earlier today; right?" That was my question to you. And you responded: "That's right." And then, if we -- to be perfectly fair, I'll read to you your answers after "that's right." You said: "A. That's right. But when we come to the site itself, then we see that it couldn't have been any different in view of the configuration of the terrain. It either could have been there or up there in Ozrenska." And then I said: "Q. Thank you for that, but I want you to focus on my questions. My next question about that map is: Do you know who made the pencil mark?" And you said: "A. I can't see [sic]. I cannot see the map." And then I directed you to your report. And then if we go down to line 18, you said: "Yes, that's the map that was cited. The working map of the Chief of Staff of the 12th Division ..." And then I said: "... you don't know who made the pencil mark, do you? And then you said: "I see those markings in blue and red, is that what you mean?" And I said: "No. I was referring to the pencil mark ..." And then you said: "There's a straight line, if that's what you mean. I don't know, but I did not mark anything on this map ..." So my question is: What's the basis for your statement that the line shifted -- your statement that we see in your report today in this case, that the line shifted towards Ivana Krndelja Street by about 100 metres?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The basis for my assertion is this red and blue line that is drawn in the working map of the Chief of Staff, and I said that in the Karadzic case, and I said it here. By going to the scene, we saw that that's how it should have been or that the forces of the Army of Republika Srpska were up in Ozrenska because of the configuration of the terrain. Perhaps that's why it was moved a bit forward. I don't see what -- what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When did you go to the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was there in 2010 and 2011, I think, in May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'm sorry. It was in 2012, in December. 2012, in December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And by going to the scene you established that the confrontation line has shifted 100 metres? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I established that this line, as it was drawn here on this working map, corresponds to the situation in the field. We had information, and I mentioned that during the examination-in-chief, about the place where the trenches of the Army of Republika Srpska were. And the configuration of the terrain is such that you have Ozrenska Street and then there is a kind of hole, and then there is a flat part and then again there is a slope, and these lines actually indicate that situation, meaning that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have answered the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, that does correspond to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I then understand that you went to the location exactly where these lines, the blue and the red ones, are, you visited those locations, or did you view it from the location where the mother and the girl were when they were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I was there. I went to that location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you saw that it had shifted 100 metres? How did you ... how did you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I wanted to double-check whether this line, since it's pulled forward, whether it was logical for it to be that way. And I saw for myself that that's how the terrain was. It had to be drawn the way it was. Either that or they were up in Ozrenska because of the terrain that forms a kind of hole, indentation. Nobody would enter that. It doesn't make sense to have positions there. So the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska were at the exposed parts and then the slope comes. And it doesn't make any sense to have your positions on the slope because it would put them in a dangerous position. There was a 200-metre difference between the warring parties because of the slope, and it's not logical to be there because you do not want do expose yourself to the danger, and that's why this line makes sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you say: Logic tells me that it is likely that it's correct. Did you read any specific evidence about where the separation line was at the time? Witnesses who have testified bout what was at Ozrenska Street, what was -- how far it was away, did you read any evidence on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes? Okay. What did -- then please tell us what you read exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to what I read, that the witnesses said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Witness, first tell us what you read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read where the trenches of the Army of Republika Srpska were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no. You are telling us what you read. But I would like to know which witness statement or testimony or whatever. What is it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, yes, which document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What is it exactly what you read about ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read the witness -- statement by RM147, he was a Prosecution witness. And I think also the transcript, a part of the transcript, I read that. I read the transcript of a witness in the Karadzic case, Slobodan -- I can't remember. Maybe I'll remember it later. So they described more or less where the positions and the trenches were, and that was something that was of help to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was it consistent with these lines or ... did they confirm the accuracy of these lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not mention or confirm the entire line but they did confirm these exposed positions, with the help of photographs as well. And that was of help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: One little question. Was this map an operative map as at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to what it says, the map was not an operative one. It was drafted later, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: We are going to come back to the question of the shift, but I'd like to go right into a Scheduled Incident, and that's F-5. Now -- and that's at English page 121 and B/C/S page 120. So just so you know, I'm always just going to give you the page references where the sections on that incidents begin. And it covers paragraphs 80 to 94. Now, in the video that we saw yesterday relating to this incident, you remember we saw the victim standing on the place where she says she got shot and pointing down the road. So you remember seeing that on the left-hand side of the screen -- and we can show the video again if you want but we can also go to your report. On the left-hand side of the screen there's an elevation supported by a concrete wall, and on the right-hand side of the screen of the video we saw yesterday there was a hill with a radio tower. You remember seeing that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you saw the victim yesterday pointing down that road, that natural tunnel, to indicate the direction of fire from which she was shot; right? We saw it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And you said what you could establish with certainty is that the positions of the VRS were visible from that place that was shown by the victim. And that was at transcript page 40485, lines 22 to 24. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Right. Let's have a look at 65 ter number 33226.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Maybe what we could -- yes, if we could just enlarge that.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So what we've got on this page is, on the top part of the page, exhibit -- we have an image that appears on page 29 of Mr. Van der Weijden's report, which is P1130, and on the bottom is we have part of your image 88. If you want to go to page 128 in your report, you can see that. It's the little yellow box that's on the top right of your image 188 [sic]. Now, that blue dot on Mr. Van der Weijden's report, the image from Mr. Van der Weijden's report, marks the location at which we saw the victim standing yesterday, the place where she was shot. And you know, because you studied his report, that Mr. Van der Weijden drew those based on GPS co-ordinates. Now, on the bottom right is your location. And what we did using Google Earth, which you use a lot, with the image on the left, is we mapped out the difference between the actual incident location as identified in Mr. Van der Weijden's report, which is the blue dot, and where you argue it happened. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some matters were announced as to be raised at this moment. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to alert the Court, I have one and Mr. McCloskey will raise the other matter. My matter concerns the request by the Trial Chamber on Tuesday about whether the Prosecution wished to address remarks by Mr. Lukic about MFI P7527, which was an Official Note by an AID official based on information provided by Dusan Bilcar about the death of his wife Ratka. And the Trial Chamber gave us until today to do so. As it turns out, Your Honours, a review of the background to the tendering of this document is quite illuminating. The document was tendered on September 1st, and at that time Mr. Lukic objected that the Official Note had not been signed by Mr. Bilcar. That's at transcript 38580 through -81. Somehow suggesting that there is something suspect when an Official Note is signed by the official who prepared the note, rather than the source of the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you just for a second. I think it was 38580 through -81 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. If I misstated, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Otherwise you would have talked about for more than 70 pages. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Because at that time there was a question about whether the attachments to the Official Note were available for review, the Trial Chamber decided to defer admission until it heard further from the Prosecution about those documents. And in the same court session, the Prosecution advised that the two attachments, an excerpt from the death registry and a death certificate, were now uploaded. And that's found at 38598. The Trial Chamber then stated it would MFI the documents pending translation of the annexes; that's 38599. And at that point, the Trial Chamber asked Mr. Lukic whether in light of the nature of the annexes and their relationship to the Official Note he still maintained the objection. He advised that he did so, explained his position again, and the Trial Chamber noted in response that these points "didn't deprive it," meaning the Official Note, "from its probative value." But also noted that it understood that the objection stood and it would therefore decide on admissibility formally when the translations arrived. That's 38600 to -01. Two days later, on the 3rd of September, Ms. Stewart advised the Trial Chamber and the parties by e-mail that the full translation for the entirety of the document, including the annexes, had been received and those were now uploaded in e-court under doc ID 0105-8653-1-ET. As far as we're aware, nothing further happened until this past Tuesday when Mr. Lukic decided to expand his objections without either notice to us or presumably notice to the Trial Chamber and then objected that there was no number or protocol. It was not clear to him to whom the report was addressed, the Official Note was addressed, and that the interview was not attached. Now, apart from what I would consider the procedural irregularity of unexpectedly reopening the argument on the issue, the objections are also substantively groundless. As mentioned, it borders on the frivolous, I would suggest, to state or suggest that the note should have been signed by the person providing the information rather than the official who wrote the note. And that point is perhaps best exemplified by the fact that this very day we received a notice of documents that Mr. Lukic intends to seek to tender which included an Official Note signed by the official and not the witness. That's 65 ter 09985. Further, with respect to the arguments more recently advanced by Mr. Lukic regarding no number or indication of intended recipient, et cetera, evidence in this case, that's P4889, page 8, and other documents that the parties are both aware of, and that would be, for example, 65 ter 32988, make clear that the format of P7527 was the customary format; that is, no case number or protocol number, no particular person to whom it was to be sent, and it was signed by the official rather than the informational source. Further, the Defence itself has tendered analogous or similar documents; that is, Official Notes which were not signed by either the person who -- by the person who provided the information but instead by the official who prepared the Official Note, that do not bear a number or a protocol, and that have no indication of a specific intended recipient. And those, for example, would be D00824 and D00825. The Defence should therefore be well aware of the fact that this is scarcely an anomaly and, in any event, does not deprive the document of probative value to bar admission. So as the Trial Chamber itself noted in early September, the Defence arguments do not deprive the document of probative value and it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And we see it displayed in the top image of page 2 of 65 ter number 33332 in green. So, Mr. Poparic, your markings of the field of fire which you argue takes into account -- or exposes the victim to fire from Bosnian-held territory actually ignores the visual evidence of that narrow tunnel up the road and the actual field of fire shows almost no line of sight from Bosnian-held territory at all. We see it clearly here, don't we?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that and it is incorrect. As I said, I --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No -- Mr. Poparic --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- drew the line close to the building but --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I just asked you -- I just asked if you could -- if you could see the difference here and you've answered the question. Now, I showed this image, this identical image to you in the Karadzic case and in that case you agreed, at transcript pages 39234, line 24 to 39235, line 2, you agreed that the area you marked is perhaps wider than the one marked by Van der Weijden. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Now, you admitted in the Karadzic case there was some deviation with Van der Weijden, and that's at 39235, lines 3 and 4, and this is all, by the way, at 65 ter number 39270 [sic], pages 72 and 73. You admitted some deviation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When you read numbers, you should slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: 65 -- pardon me. 65 ter number 32790, pages 72 and 73.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So you saw --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we just have one image on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: You saw this in the Karadzic case. You admitted there was some deviation, but what you did in your report for this case is, admitting the deviation, you still haven't corrected it. You filed exactly the same images; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: And those -- your image crosses over geographical boundaries and doubles up the field of fire that actually exists from the point the victim says she was shot at; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain? I stand by what I said in the Karadzic case. I allow for the possibility that the boundaries may be wider, whoever set them. I guess it was Mr. Van der Weijden. That is irrelevant. What is relevant whether there was space in either of the controlled territories from which the location would visible. The median purple line follows the middle of the street, no matter whether it is moved up or down in relation to the point you marked. That is the middle of the street. Now whether it is on the left or right, in my view, is not important. I did not change that. As I said in the Karadzic case, that is my view. However, there is an area in both VRS-controlled area and in ABiH-controlled area. That is correct. I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you the following. Do you -- are you telling us that from the yellow-dot position, as you thought was the correct one, that obstructions by buildings, by the terrain, et cetera, are exactly the same as the obstructions you would find at the spot where Ramiza Kundo said she was hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I explained a moment ago, but you did not understand obviously. The terrain is such that the buildings in front, as we can see in the corner, do not present an obstacle in relation to the place where Ms. Kundo was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you measured that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw it. I didn't have to measure it. I could see it. It's visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if you look at your own image 85, you see that? That's a still from the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's on page 123 in English, if you want to display it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 123 in English. Now, is the slope there so steep that the terrain would be no obstacle whatsoever irrespective of whether you follow the road, or left of the road, or right of the road, it would make no difference whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, I'm not asserting that. I said that in the context of the sketch. To the right, behind Mr. Hogan, where we can see these containers ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where the containers are, there's a slope, a pile of earth, which obstructs the area from view. On the left-hand side, there is this plateau --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that give an obstruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Stop. Is there a similar obstruction from the location you identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I took that into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I -- I asked you whether there's a similar obstruction there. Because you -- from that point, you gave a very wide angle from which there was a line of vision, which suggests that there was no obstruction, no obstruction of sight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not agree. If we look at the sketch, it all ends in a very sharp angle of a triangle which enters the street and perhaps goes over the fence because it's very low. So depending on the distance, one could potentially see over it. Ms. Edgerton objected to the width of the area. I told you I did not determine the width precisely. If it was needed, I would have engaged land surveyors or someone of that sort to measure it. What was important for me was to see whether it was visible from either of the territories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, therefore, the width is very important, the width of the area where there is a line of sight. Because I didn't find any photographs from your point looking downwards, whether there's any obstruction, yes or no. We see in this still from the video that both to the left of the street and right of the street, looking from where these persons are standing, that there are obstructions, considerable obstructions of sight.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. On the left- and right-hand side. But on the diagram, on the sketch, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. What I'd like to know is whether from your location, whether we find similar obstructions and whether you have taken pictures of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. What do you mean when you say my location? Down below in the field?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 130 metres away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not the location I had in mind, the one that is depicted. It's a technical error. I analysed this particular case. I did not even consider --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You drew the lines and the angle with unobstructed view from there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I assert that from this location there are areas on both sides from which it is visible. They may not be too big, but they are there. That is what I wanted to say. As for the width of each area, I didn't determine that. One may be critical about how wide it is, and I did not precisely determine that because I thought it irrelevant. Why would I be doing that? Mr. Van der Weijden also approximated. He did invest a bit more effort trying to sort out angles but it's also just an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Basically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you agree that what you observed and the sketch you have drawn from a wrong position gives us not a good idea of what the line of sights because it is assessed - not even measured - from a wrong location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that it was mistakenly taken. I depicted that location and the same direction. It is the very same direction. The only thing that can be open for discussion is the width.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the width leads to whether it is area under control of the BiH or the VRS. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please -- I'm looking at the clock. We should have stopped already.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could I just have this document 65 ter 33332 as a Prosecution exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7593, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is both -- oh, no. It's one -- yes. That's how many pages? Two pages --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Two pages, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One separate and then the overlay on the second one. Yes. Admitted into evidence. Witness, we'll take a break and we will resume -- since we're not sitting on Fridays, we'll resume on Monday, the 2nd of November, 2015, at 9.30 in the morning, and we'd like to see you back then. And I instruct you, as I did before, that you should not communicate with whomever about your testimony in whatever way, and we'd like to see you back. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Upon adjourning, I add for the parties that it will be in this same courtroom, I, on the 2nd of November.
